title: When Weak Fields Aren't Weak: Post-Newtonian effective theory and the Dark Matter Puzzle (Galoppo, Torrieri)
efc_relevance: Gravity Research Foundation 2026 essay arguing that the post-Newtonian expansion of GR is not generically reliable in many-body relativistic dynamics: absence of globally conserved charges in the region of interest plus non-integrability can drive strong sensitivity to angular-momentum exchange across inhomogeneous curvature, invalidating naive PN power counting. Derives an explicit breakdown criterion. Extends the Galoppo–Buchert–Mourier backreaction programme (arXiv:2605.05454) and gives EFC a theoretical lever: if PN truncations are unreliable on galactic and cluster scales, the standard 'GR + DM halo' inference is itself effective-theory limited, opening a principled niche for EFC's entropy-flow source term as a non-PN correction rather than a new field.
ledger_action: Add to External Research Ledger under cluster alternative-cosmology/backreaction; cross-reference arXiv:2605.05454 (Galoppo et al. 2026 local backreaction) and update that row with the PN-breakdown extension; new gap row (gap theory-pn-breakdown-efc) — EFC must publish where in (r, v) parameter space its S(r,t) corrections become comparable to the PN truncation error identified here.
